title: Grothendieck rings of near-Tambara–Yamagami fusion categories
authors: Jingcheng Dong, Sébastien Palcoux and Kai Wang
summary: Determines the possible Grothendieck rings for fusion categories containing a nonpointed Tambara–Yamagami subcategory and exactly one additional simple object. The analysis produces three based rings and gives categorifications for all three, including an explicit unitary group-theoretical realization.

title: Classification of vanishing fusion rings of rank four
authors: Jingcheng Dong, Sébastien Palcoux and Arnaud Plessis
summary: Classifies rank-four fusion rings in which a multiplication matrix is singular. The integral classification produces infinitely many simple examples, rules out 1-Frobenius simple integral fusion rings at rank four, and also yields a classification of rank-four Burnside fusion rings.

title: Triangular prism equations for near-group categories: algebraic solutions and a unitary conjecture
authors: Huixuan He, Zhengwei Liu, Fan Lu, Sébastien Palcoux and Yunxiang Ren
summary: Develops triangular prism equations for near-group fusion rules and constructs cyclic solutions using hyperbolic gamma functions. Galois conjugation connects these solutions to pseudo-unitary categories, while the remaining unitarity question leads to a real-multiplication conjecture related to Stark’s conjectures.

title: Classifying Grothendieck rings of pivotal fusion categories of rank four
authors: Jingcheng Dong, Sébastien Palcoux and Arnaud Plessis
summary: Classifies the Grothendieck rings of pivotal complex fusion categories of rank four: exactly fifteen rings occur, each with a unitary categorification. Central induction and Frobenius–Schur indicators give a uniform dimension bound, while arithmetic and twist obstructions provide exact exclusion certificates.

title: Local Ocneanu rigidity for separable algebra objects
authors: Tinhinane Amina Azzouz, Mainak Ghosh and Sébastien Palcoux
summary: Establishes local rigidity and effective finiteness for separable algebra objects and their homomorphisms. Exchange relations turn Frobenius subalgebra questions into idempotent geometry, with applications to coideal subalgebras, intermediate operator algebras, and quantitative bounds for intermediate subfactors.

title: Sharp bounds for intervals in finite subgroup lattices
authors: Sébastien Palcoux and Pablo Spiga
summary: Gives sharp bounds on the number of intermediate subgroups between a subgroup and a finite group. A weighted packing inequality removes the polynomial factor from earlier relative bounds, with both the exponent and leading constant attained asymptotically by elementary abelian examples.

title: A new criterion for integral modular categorification
authors: Jingcheng Dong and Sébastien Palcoux
summary: Introduces an efficient necessary criterion for integral modular categorification, generalizing an argument of Etingof, Nikshych, and Ostrik. The criterion completes the classification of categorifiable integral modular data up to rank fourteen, and up to rank twenty-five in the odd-dimensional case.

title: Frobenius subalgebra lattices in tensor categories
authors: Mainak Ghosh and Sébastien Palcoux
summary: Extends Watatani’s finiteness theorem to Frobenius subalgebra lattices in monoidal categories under suitable coherence and positivity assumptions. Formal angles, ambient selfduality, and exchange relations connect tensor-categorical rigidity with applications to Hopf algebras, C*-algebras, and quantum arithmetic.

title: Triangular Prism Equations and Categorification
authors: Zhengwei Liu, Sébastien Palcoux, Yunxiang Ren and Gert Vercleyen
summary: Introduces triangular prism equations for fusion categories through oriented graphical calculus. In the spherical setting, these equations are equivalent to the pentagon equations after a change of basis. Localization then gives practical categorification criteria and resolves remaining unitary simple integral examples within specified bounds.

title: Classifying integral Grothendieck rings up to rank 5 and beyond
authors: Max A. Alekseyev, Winfried Bruns, Jingcheng Dong and Sébastien Palcoux
summary: Classifies integral Grothendieck rings up to rank five and treats several higher-rank cases. Egyptian fractions, Normaliz computations, and induction to the Drinfeld center combine arithmetic restrictions with exact constructions and exclusions, including examples beyond the Isaacs property.
